description: On the left is a vertical memory module. Two gray lines connect its black chip area to the memory grid on the right. The physical chips and the dark cells marking used space in the grid represent different levels of detail.

The grid has five rows and eight columns. The rows start at 0x0000, 0x0010, 0x0020, 0x0030, and 0x0040, with column offsets 00 through 07. Ellipses at the right and bottom indicate additional cells. Light cells are available and dark cells are in use. An available cell does not necessarily contain 0.

frames.explanation: Add a row's starting address and a column offset to locate a cell. For example, 0x0020 plus offset 04 gives 0x0024, which holds the value 2. The two reads below the grid correspond to the two rows in the table. An address identifies a location, and the data is the content stored there. The grid illustrates addressing rather than the chip's physical circuit layout.
frames.title: Accessing memory by address

summary: Add the column offset to the row's starting address to locate a memory cell and read its data.
